concerns.text: The plan proposes using 'exact match of the solution string' (GSM8K) or 'action sequence' (MiniGrid) as the ground truth for token-level validity. This construct validity flaw means a token is labeled 'valid' only if the *entire* sequence is correct. In autoregressive generation, a single early error invalidates the rest of the sequence, making the 'validity' label a proxy for 'sequence success' rather than 'token correctness'. This conflates the dependent variable (token validity) with the sequence outcome, rendering the logistic regression unable to distinguish between a model that is uncertain about a correct token vs. one that has already failed. The analysis cannot answer the research question 'does entropy predict token validity' under this labeling scheme.

The plan acknowledges ~250k token-level observations but treats them as independent samples in a standard logistic regression. This violates the assumption of independence (construct validity) because tokens within a sequence are highly correlated (temporal dependency) and share the same sequence-level validity label. Without a Mixed-Effects Model (GLMM) with a random intercept for `sequence_id` (as hinted in `contracts/analysis_result.schema.yaml` but not explicitly detailed in the analysis plan), the standard errors will be underestimated, inflating Type I error rates and invalidating the p-values and FDR corrections.

The plan relies on 'TinyLlama' or 'Qwen1.5-0.5B' for GSM8K and MiniGrid. These models are known to have poor performance on GSM8K (often <10% accuracy) and MiniGrid. If the model fails to generate valid sequences >90% of the time, the dataset will be overwhelmingly skewed towards 'invalid' labels (class imbalance). A logistic regression on such a skewed dataset with a weak signal (entropy) may fail to converge or produce uninterpretable odds ratios, making the study underpowered to detect the specific effect of entropy on the rare 'valid' tokens.
